issues.description: The template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java does not provide the expected Farm class declared in the problem statement/UML and shown in the solution. Instead it declares a class named AnimalFarm and contains duplicated/malformed package and class blocks (including an embedded 'package' line and a second class declaration inside a method). This structural mismatch and syntax error prevents students from compiling and implementing the intended Farm class and will cause confusion about the required class name and structure.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the template contents of src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java with a single, well-formed class named Farm (matching the UML and solution). Ensure there is only one package declaration at the top, no embedded duplicate package/class blocks, and the class provides the expected fields and method stubs (e.g., private List<Animal> animals; constructor initializing the list; addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, singFarmSong methods). This will align the template with the problem statement and solution and allow students to compile and implement the exercise.

issues.description: The template defines a public class named 'AnimalFarm' (in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) while the problem statement and the solution expect a class named 'Farm'. The provided Main.java in the template also instantiates 'Farm'. This naming mismatch prevents students from mapping the required 'Farm' concept from the problem to the template implementation and will cause confusion and compilation errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template class 'AnimalFarm' to 'Farm' (and ensure the public class name matches the file name), so it aligns with the problem statement and the solution. Update any references in Main.java or other template files to use 'Farm' consistently.
